GR-001.statement: Revocation MUST be an explicit action separate from disable/re-enable, identifying the exact application, current version and bounded reason before acceptance.

GR-002.statement: Acceptance and explicit continuation MUST require current account eligibility, current `grants.revoke` and fresh MFA. No other application permission implies revocation.

GR-003.statement: The system MUST protect administrator/pilot and unmanaged applications by durable identity as well as reserved names; expired credentials alone MUST NOT exclude cleanup.

GR-004.statement: Submission MUST require an already disabled application. It MUST remain disabled while any revocation job is incomplete, including stopped/failed work. Only successful reconciliation permits a separate explicit re-enable; completion MUST NOT automatically enable it. No submission implicitly exercises disable permission.

GR-005.statement: The selected scope MUST include eligible stored authorizations and tokens independently, including tokens without an authorization link. Already invalid records MUST NOT become valid. Other applications and target credentials/configuration are preserved.

GR-006.statement: Acceptance MUST persist immutable intent, approving actor, reason, target, scope, time and correlation, returning a durable job reference and protected status location. Recorded approval MUST NOT retain or replay sign-in credentials or bearer tokens.

GR-007.statement: Accepted work MUST continue after sign-out or original MFA expiry while rechecking current account eligibility and actual revocation permission for every batch. The actor of the currently effective acceptance/continuation approval is checked; earlier approvers remain immutable history. Concurrent authority changes and commits MUST have a proved serial order.

GR-008.statement: Each bounded batch MUST commit native changes, exact progress and its audit together. A failed batch MUST NOT erase or misreport earlier committed progress.

GR-009.statement: Restart and competing workers MUST preserve exactly accounted committed progress. Unknown commit outcomes MUST be reconciled against durable state before further work.

GR-010.statement: Repeated identical submissions MUST recover the same accepted operation within the documented idempotency window, scoped to actor, action and exact target. Duplicate recovery MUST recheck current account/access and MUST NOT disclose another actor's job. Reuse for different intent MUST conflict. Submission retries MUST NOT create duplicate work or duplicate acceptance audit records.

GR-011.statement: Status MUST show committed authorization/token counts, pending/completed/stopped state and bounded safe errors. Unknown totals MUST NOT be shown as exact percentages. Reads MUST require current `applications.read` and `grants.revoke`, not identifier possession.

GR-012.statement: Durably stopped authority-denied or failed work MUST require explicit fresh confirmation to continue its fixed remaining scope; no silent revival after authority restoration. Recovery MUST preserve approval history, completed batches and target restrictions. Process restart alone is not an authority failure and may resume work still eligible under GR-007. If storage prevents recording a stop, report unavailable/unknown rather than claiming it stopped. Late failure recording stops incomplete work under the same approval even when progress advanced, but never overwrites a later approval or terminal success.

GR-013.statement: The UI MUST distinguish acceptance from completion and explain that revoking stored authority cannot erase offline tokens or sessions owned by other applications.

GR-014.statement: Committed-entry revocation enforcement MUST meet the existing five-second platform boundary requirement where that entry is validated. This does not promise whole-job completion within five seconds or invent a supported resource audience.

GR-015.statement: The existing local-demo entry point MUST support the complete action/status journey. Keyboard, focus, light/dark and retained browser behavior remain required.

SC-001.statement: Every accepted operation has a recoverable reference; every duplicate matching submission by the same currently authorized actor in the documented window returns that same operation, with no cross-actor disclosure.

SC-002.statement: At completion, 100% of eligible records in the fixed scope are revoked; zero unrelated records, credentials or application configuration fields are changed.

SC-003.statement: Sign-out and original MFA expiry do not interrupt eligible accepted work; account/permission loss prevents the next batch after that change takes effect.

SC-004.statement: Across injected failures and restart scenarios, reported counts match independently observed committed changes, with zero uncommitted successes reported.

SC-005.statement: Relevant platform validation rejects committed revoked entries within five seconds, measured from batch commit, while unaffected control entries remain usable.

SC-006.statement: The local demonstration completes submission, progress, recovery and result journeys through the ordinary application UI without scripts or manual database changes.

T001.limit: Design authorization/review is documentary; test identities alone cannot establish it.
